newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia stocks jump record 7.74 pct, more ahead.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia stocks jump record 7.74 pct, more ahead.

text.p: The Slovenian blue-chip SBI index surged 7.74 percent or 103.81 points on Wednesday to record its biggest daily rise to date, with market sentiment buoyed by a relaxation of rules for foreign investors.

"If there are no unpleasant surprises regarding investment rules or Slovenia's plan to join the European Union as soon as possible, the index could reach 2,000 points by the end of the year," a trader said.
The central bank has enabled foreigners to invest without incurring extra bank charges provided they hold onto a share for at least seven years or trade among themselves.
The SBI index rose 103.81 points to 1,444.4 points. The previous record jump was recorded on February 17, when the index went up by 97.73 points.
In 10 consecutive days of gains the blue-chip index has advanced 21.35 percent.
Traders said international investors should come back en masse following the central bank's decree.
"Our market is the only one where such a good firms are so underpriced," said Primoz Kokol, a trader at brokerage Start.
But some market participants cautioned gains could be pared if Slovenia failed to ratify its association agreement with the European Union.
The ratification of the treaty, signed in June last year and a precondition for full EU memebership, is expected by the end of this month.
Overall 20 shares rose, two were flat and six untraded. Turnover more than doubled to 395.3 million tolars.
Traders said, petrol trader Petrol, drug makers Lek and Krka along with food producers Droga and Kolinska, were the most attractive shares for foreign buyers.
Petrol was the most active share, up 8.43 percent to 20,580 tolars on volume of 5,969, for total turnover of 122.2 million tolars.
Bank Probanka was the top gainer, jumping 12.29 percent to 22,850 tolars on volume of 842 shares.
Market participants said the bank was helped higher by news last week that Daiwa Europe had been given the green light by the Bank of Slovenia to buy 2.94 percent of Probanka.
Pharmaceutical company Lek surged 8.69 percent to 29,020 tolars on volume of 2,028 shares.
Its rival Krka, which is listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) section of Ljubljana bourse, jumped 18.9 percent or 3,750 tolars to 23,540 tolars on volume of 17,451 shares.
Droga rose 6.67 percent to 32,000 tolars and Kolinska was up 6.62 percent to 2,239 tolars. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
